notes.title: Patch 0.8.6.1 is online!
notes.content:
[b]Patch Notes - Version 0.8.6.1[/b]

Greetings, fellow game developers!

I'm thrilled to present the latest patch for [b]"Software Company"[/b], where I've been hard at work fixing bugs, implementing exciting features, and incorporating valuable feedback from our passionate community. 

Let's dive into the details of [i]Version 0.8.6.1[/i].

[i][b]Bug Fixes[/b][/i]

[list]
[*] I've resolved an issue where certain buttons were unresponsive, ensuring smooth navigation and uninterrupted gameplay.
[*] I've tackled problems related to UI font scaling and tooltips appearing out of place, resulting in a visually cohesive and polished user interface.
[*] Previously, reviews were only generated when players accessed the review page directly. Now, reviews will be correctly instantiated when browsing the UGN Website, creating a more realistic game environment.
[/list]

[i][b]Enhancements and Additions[/b][/i]

[list]
[*] To assist you in improving your game design skills, I've added helpful hints to the review-overview screen. These hints will provide subtle guidance on which slider settings were effective and which ones could have been adjusted differently. With these clues, you'll gain valuable insights into creating more successful games.
[*] I understand the importance of feedback in honing your skills. Therefore, I've introduced a Feedback section on the review-overview screen. This feature will provide information on good, missing, and unnecessary features in your games. Leverage this knowledge to refine your game development strategies.
[*] Introducing the Company-Charts page on the UGN Website! Now, you can easily track your progress and compare your studio's performance against others. Witness the fierce competition in the race for the title of the best video game studio in the world. Furthermore, each AI studio now boasts its own unique company logo, enhancing the overall visual experience.
[/list]

[i][b]Upcoming Changes[/b][/i]

I've heard your suggestions and I'm actively working on making exciting adjustments to the game's economy and i have started to implement a random-event system to keep you busy while waiting for your neweset creations being finished. 

Further, the introduction of the company-charts is a base for a soon-to-be implementation of an ingame stock market, where you can invest in other software companies or buy them up all together.

These changes aim to introduce more excitement and variety in multiple playthroughs, ensuring each session feels fresh and engaging. Stay tuned for more information on these upcoming enhancements!

As always, I sincerely appreciate your continued support and feedback throughout the development of "Software Company." Your dedication and enthusiasm inspire me to deliver the best possible gaming experience. As always, please keep sharing your thoughts and suggestions on Discord and the steam community page. Together, let's shape the future of game development!

Stay tuned for more updates and happy game developing!

Sascha

notes.title: Patchnotes 0.8.6.0 - The first content Update is here!
notes.content:
[b]Changelog - First Content Update[/b]

Hello players! I am excited to bring you the first content update for [i][b]"Software Company"[/b][/i]. This update includes various fixes, changes, and new features to enhance your gameplay experience. 

Thank you for your continued support and valuable feedback. Here's what's new:

[b]Fixes[/b]

[list]
[*] Fixed an issue where multiple of the same resolutions were displayed in the resolution settings dropdown. Additionally, the minimum resolution for the game is now capped at 1280*720 pixels.
[*] Addressed a bug where some data was carried over from a previous game when starting a new game after returning to the main menu.
[*] Resolved an issue with loading saved games from the in-game load menu. Players can now correctly load saved games without having to go back to the main menu or quit the game.
[*] Fixed avatar generation for all character models. These avatars will be used in various areas throughout the game.
[*] 
[/list]

[b]Changes[/b]

[list]
[*] [b]NEW[/b]: Complete UI overhaul with a sleeker design, new graphics, and more!
[*] [b]NEW[/b]: Added an "UI-Scaling" option in the settings menu. Now you can scale the UI up to improve readability on lower resolutions.
[*][b]NEW[/b]: Introducing a 25x game speed option. Please note that this option is highly experimental and might cause glitches on weaker systems. Use with caution!
[*][b]NEW[/b]: Select the box art for your games in the "Create new project" menu. While the game still assigns colors randomly, you can now choose the background picture, font style, and font shape of your box art. Enjoy the new level of customization!
[*][b]NEW[/b]: Cancel games in development. If you change your mind or encounter unforeseen circumstances, you now have the option to cancel a project.
[*][b]NEW[/b]: Add or remove developers during active development. Adjust your team as needed to optimize your projects.
[*]The version of the game when a save file was created has been added to the save game information displayed in the load screens.
[*]User settings are now stored in a separate file. Your preferences will not be reset with each game update.
[*]Several new conversations have been added to enhance the overall experience.
[*]The "release" button from the contact window has been removed. Players are now required to call the employee they wish to release and confront them personally, dealing with their guilt in person.
[/list]

[b]Known Issues[/b]

[list]
[*]The new font may encounter difficulties displaying country-specific characters and may revert back to a fallback font.
[*]Extended gameplay sessions, especially on weaker systems, may result in decreased performance. This is caused by background logging to facilitate bug and error identification. We will gradually remove most, if not all, of these logging protocols in future updates. For now, if your game's performance becomes sluggish, simply save and restart the game to reset the logging scripts and restore smooth gameplay.
[/list]

Thank you for your patience and support as i continue to improve [i][b]"Software Company"[/b][/i]. I hope you enjoy the new update and look forward to bringing you more exciting features in the future!

Regards,

Sascha

notes.title: Dev-Diaries #2: The first Content-Update is around the corner!
notes.content:
Hello, [b]Software Company[/b] players!

I'm thrilled to bring you the latest developer update for the highly anticipated content update, [i][b]version 0.8.6[/b][/i]. 

As you know, [b]"Software Company"[/b] is currently in its early access phase, and I want to express my gratitude for your incredible continued support and valuable feedback. Your passion for the game has been the driving force behind my continuous efforts to improve and expand the experience.

One common theme in your feedback has been the desire for more content. I've heard you loud and clear, and I'm excited to announce that significant progress has been made in resolving the savegame bugs that have been causing frustration among players. I'm happy to inform you that these issues are now almost completely fixed, ensuring a smoother and more seamless gaming experience. [i]Your progress is now in safer hands![/i]

Now, let's delve into the key features of the upcoming update, starting with a complete [b]UI overhaul[/b]. I've transformed the game's user interface from a functional design to a cleaner and more modern look. This new UI not only provides a better visual experience but also offers more intuitive control over the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41321079/38840b6f53143e3142d7dc76fbc174620c1fd9c8.jpg[/img]

I've taken the time to relocate certain elements to more logical positions, enhancing the usability and making it easier for you to navigate through the different aspects of running your software company. I can't wait for you to see the improvements!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41321079/070cbbfdc36ebd0b69b38e4e9aa0ba6362fa15a9.jpg[/img]

In addition to the UI overhaul, I'm introducing exciting [b]new gameplay features[/b] in version 0.8.6. One of the most significant additions is the ability for you to [b]add or remove developers from ongoing game developments[/b]. This feature empowers you to adjust the quality of a game by allocating or reallocating your development resources. 
Whether you need to free up developers for other projects or want to give that extra boost to a particular game, now you have the power to do so. [i]Flexibility and control are in your hands![/i]

Another much-requested feature is the ability to [b]cancel game developments[/b]. I understand that the market can be unpredictable, and sometimes you need to react swiftly to market changes. With the new update, you'll have the option to cancel a game's development if you see that it no longer aligns with your strategy or if you spot a new trend that demands your attention. [i]This addition allows you to adapt and make strategic decisions in real-time, maximizing your chances of success in the dynamic software industry.[/i]

Of course, version 0.8.6 also includes several [b]other bug fixes and improvements[/b] based on your feedback. I've resolved the bugs that occurred when starting a new game after returning from a loaded one to the main menu, ensuring a seamless transition between different game sessions. [i]For a complete list of all the bug fixes and improvements, I'll provide detailed patch notes upon release.[/i]

I'm incredibly excited about this upcoming content 

- which will go live on the [b]upcoming weekend[/b] - 

update, and I want to express my deepest gratitude for your support and patience. Your feedback has been instrumental in shaping the game, and I'm committed to delivering the best possible experience for you.

[i]Stay tuned for more announcements and release details. I can't wait to see you dive into the improved world of "Software Company" in version 0.8.6!

[b]Thank you once again for being part of this incredible journey with me.[/b]
[/i]
Best regards,
Sascha

notes.title: Hotfix #4 is online!
notes.content:
[hr][/hr]
[u][b]Attention:[/b][/u] To ensure that some changes take effect, I recommend starting a new game when updating to version [b]0.8.5.14[/b]. Save games made before this version of the patch may not load correctly, and while they might still work, they may result in unwanted glitches.

If you encounter any issues with save games made before this version, please note that I may not be able to provide support for them.

I always strive to make older saves still viable with each patch. However, depending on the changes, it is possible that older saves will stop working from time to time. I aim to keep these occasions as rare as possible.

To avoid confusion with older save files, I suggest going to 

[i]"C:\Users\[b]Your Username[/b]\AppData\LocalLow\InkDev Studios\Software Company" [/i]

and deleting any save games stored there (files that end with *.dat) before starting the game for the first time after the update.

[hr][/hr]

[b]#FIXES:[/b]

[list]
[*] Fixed some camera problems when calling people from the contacts window.
[*] Employees will now show up to work after being hired from a call made via the contacts window.
[*] Fixed an issue where sales for a game would skyrocket again when the game should actually be taken off the market. This will make the game probably a lot more challenging, especially in the beginning.
[*] Fixed an issue where values in a saved game for finished games would get messed up in some cases.
[/list]

This hotfix concludes the ongoing work of fixing issues with save games. There might be small patches fixing minor errors in the upcoming weeks. Otherwise, I will now start working on the first content update, including the highly requested UI overhaul, scalable UI, and further localization.

Thank you all for your continued support.

Sincerely,

Sascha

notes.title: Dev-Diaries #1: Fixes, Fixes, Fixes!
notes.content:
[u][b]Dear players and video game entrepreneurs,
[/b][/u]
It has been exactly 3 days since "Software Company" was released on Steam. These have been stressful, but also amazing 3 days.

On release day, the game even managed to secure the first place among EA releases for a few hours. A small success that I absolutely did not expect.

I want to thank you not only for giving "Software Company" a chance, but also for taking the existing bugs and glitches in stride and helping me eliminate many of them with constructive feedback. Currently, there are still some bugs on the list that need to be fixed, but thanks to the numerous helpful insights into your save games and logs, these problems will soon be a thing of the past.

To keep you as up-to-date as possible on the current state of development, there will be regular dev diaries like this one. In them, I will report on things I am currently working on, bugs that are being fixed, and anything that might interest you about the game's progress.

To start, I would like to inform you about the current status of some bugs, specifically problems that still occur in connection with save games.

Again, I would like to thank you for your understanding in dealing with the current problems. As a solo developer, I had limited systems available to me for testing the code for problems and bugs prior to release. Especially in the PC market, every system is unique - from hardware and installed software to the operating system. Each of these factors plays a role in whether a bug occurs or not. By submitting your save games, you have greatly increased the number of systems I could gain insight into, so fixing the small but annoying bugs in the save games is progressing quickly.

Yesterday, a small, undocumented patch was released online that was able to fix some of the biggest problems with most save games. I am currently aware of some other errors that I am working on and fixing. Once this is complete, there will be the first larger interim update in about 10 days, the content of which I will announce in the coming days. Currently, I am working on the following issues:

[hr][/hr]
[list]
[*] - Progress bars of currently developed games are not loaded correctly.
[*] - Occasionally, when loading a game, employees are not assigned their workplace correctly and diligently program in the parking lot.
[*] - Box arts are not loaded correctly, but appear as white boxes.
[*] - Some values in the individual game overview are displayed with incorrect values from time to time.
[*] - Occasionally, the game generates unintentionally unrealistic high sales for a game after it should have been taken off the market.
[/list]

[u][i]Work on the bugs mentioned above is progressing quickly, so I can already release the hotfix hopefully tomorrow afternoon.[/i][/u]
[hr][/hr]

Please continue to post reports of any further errors you discover.

Otherwise, I wish you continued fun with "Software Company"!

Best regards and [b]THANK YOU[/b]!!!

Sascha

notes.title: Hotfix #2 is online!
notes.content:
Hello everyone,

First of all, thank you all for the amazing last 24 hours. I received many nice messages and helpful reports regarding bugs and glitches. So, without further ado, here are the problems I fixed for now. The hotfix should be online as you read these patch notes:

[b]## —— Hotfix 0.8.5.12 ——[/b]
[hr][/hr]
[i][b]#Fixes[/b][/i]

- Fixed an issue where some entries in the research trees had no "available" date set and could not be researched.
- Fixed an issue, where the stats for programming, sound, graphics and design where set to 0, when loading a saved game.
- Fixed an issue where the "Review" page was skewed on some resolutions.
- Fixed an issue where the buttons in the "My Games - Overview" disappeared upon opening the window.
- Fixed an issue where the tutorial got stuck when asking the player to set the game size to "C". The tutorial should now continue once the player sets the game size accordingly.
- Corrected some spelling mistakes and improved grammar in the tutorial. (Both English & German localization)

[i][b]#Changes[/b][/i]

- Added the Microsoft .NET redistributable to the game installation. This should help players who had trouble saving the game. If you still have trouble saving/loading your saved games, please uninstall the game on Steam and redownload it.
- Changed the time given to the player to read the tutorial prompts to 20-30 seconds. This should make it easier for players to follow the tutorial's explanations. An option to skip ahead manually will be added in the first content update in May.
- Added a confirmation window that appears upon hiring a new employee. This will make it more obvious when the player has hired a new employee during a conversation.
- Added a confirmation prompt that confirms when the game has been successfully saved.

[i][b]#Known issues[/b][/i]

- Sometimes, box art is not loaded correctly when loading a saved game, and is instead displayed as white boxes.
- Errors may occur when attempting to load a game from the in-game menu. Until I address this issue in the next hotfix, I recommend loading a saved game from the main menu.

[hr][/hr]

Thank you for your support so far and enjoy the game. As always: For reporting bugs, feel free to use the games [url=https://discord.gg/xJPccw53g8]Discord[/url] or the community page here on steam.

Cheers,

Sascha

- Fixed an issue where the tutorial got stuck when asking the player to set the game size to "C". The tutorial should now continue once the player sets the game size accordingly.
- Corrected some spelling mistakes and improved grammar in the tutorial. (Both English & German localization)

tags.feature: - Added the Microsoft .NET redistributable to the game installation. This should help players who had trouble saving the game. If you still have trouble saving/loading your saved games, please uninstall the game on Steam and redownload it.

tags.balance_change: - Changed the time given to the player to read the tutorial prompts to 20-30 seconds. This should make it easier for players to follow the tutorial's explanations. An option to skip ahead manually will be added in the first content update in May.

tags.feature: - Added a confirmation window that appears upon hiring a new employee. This will make it more obvious when the player has hired a new employee during a conversation.

notes.title: EA-Roadmap for "Software Company"
notes.content:
Dear Players,

I'm excited to share with you the roadmap for the Early Access release of my game on Steam. As a solo developer, my goal is to provide a comprehensive plan for the next several months of development that will enhance the overall user experience and increase player retention rate through monthly updates with new features and bi-weekly updates with minor fixes. I expect the game to be ready for final release after 6-9 months in Early Access.

[hr][/hr]

Here's a breakdown of the key features and improvements I plan to implement, along with specific milestones and dates:

[u][b]April-May:[/b][/u]
[list]
[*] [u][i]Addition of one more map:[/i][/u] I'll include the first additional map shortly after release. This map was already planned to be included in the first EA-release but didn't quite make it. I'll make sure you guys will have the ability to buy a bigger office not too far after release, where you can hire more employees.
[*] [i][u]Bug-Fixes:[/u][/i] I hope you guys won't encounter too many bugs during your first few hours of gameplay. But those you will find will be fixed as soon as possible.
[/list]

[u][b]May - June:[/b][/u]

[list]
[*] [i][u]Bug fixes and performance improvements:[/u][/i] I'll prioritize game-breaking bugs and performance improvements during this period.
[*] [i][u]UI improvements:[/u][/i] I'll enhance the user interface to make it more intuitive and user-friendly.
[*] [i][u]More dialogue options:[/u][/i] I'll add additional dialogue options for player characters to add depth and realism to the game.
[/list]

[u][b]July - August:[/b][/u]

[list]
[*] [i][u]Company Charts:[/u][/i] I'll add a list of all active companies in a playthrough, sorted by company value, and updated every month in-game.
[*] [i][u]More maps:[/u][/i] I'll add additional maps to play on, providing players with even more options to explore.
[*] [i][u]Ability to purchase other companies:[/u][/i] I'll introduce a new feature that allows players to buy other companies, expanding their portfolio of games and employees.
[/list]

[u][b]September - October:[/b][/u]

[list]
[*] [i][u]Random game events that impact the economy:[/u][/i] I'll introduce economic crises and trends impacted by successful game genres, adding depth and unpredictability to the game.
[*] [i][u]Yearly Game Awards:[/u][/i] I'll add categories like Game of the Year, Most Financial Success, Company of the Year, Technical Breakthrough, and others to recognize the achievements of players in the game.
[*] [i][u]Game sequels:[/u][/i] I'll add the ability to create sequels for previously developed games, giving players more options for expanding their portfolio.
[/list]

[u][b]November - December:[/b][/u]

[list]
[*] [i][u]Development of own Consoles:[/u][/i] I'll introduce the ability to create and sell your own gaming consoles, adding a new level of customization to the game.
[*] [i][u]More bug fixes and performance improvements:[/u][/i] I'll continue to address any remaining bugs and performance issues to ensure a smooth and enjoyable gaming experience for everyone.
[/list]

I recognize the importance of community feedback in the development process, and I welcome any suggestions or concerns you may have. I'll be actively monitoring player retention through Steam statistics and balancing new features based on your feedback.

I understand that unforeseen delays can occur, but I plan to mitigate these risks by building a buffer in my timeline and communicating any delays with the community. My goal is to create a game that is both enjoyable and engaging for all players, and I look forward to continuing this journey with you.

Thank you for your continued support.

Best regards,

Sascha, Developer of [i][b]Software Company[/b][/i]

notes.title: Development-Blog #1: Der Weg zum "closed" Playtest.
notes.content:
[b]Weekly development-blogs from now on until the start of the "closed" playtest scheduled towards the end of november[/b]

From now on you will have the opportunity to get some insights in the development-progress of [b]Software Company[/b].

I want to start this weeks edition by announcing the [b]closed playtest[/b] at the end of november.
This will give me the opportunity to test the then up-to-date version of the game together with the players and take the feedback into the future steps of the development-process.

More on that coming up here of course, but also keep an eye open for the button on the shoppage, where you can sign up for the playtest, once it is available.

Further i want to give you a weekly insight in the current "to-do" things during the development of the game.

This week is all about the research & development part of the game , internaly also known as the "skill-tree".
Because what better way to call and design it, in a game where you develop videogames, then the famous skilltree we all know and love from multiple RPGs, right?

I don't want to spoil too much of course, but all in all you can describe the system like the following:

- The different research-sections are devided in different parts. Right now in engine features, gameplay features and genres&themes.

- Every part gives you different areas to develop new things, like in this small example:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41321079/5c8c4576421d354995f712bc28e2291b158925a9.png[/img]

The different options available to you vary depended on the progress in the game (aka what year it is), your former design-choices and individual dependencies of the elements among each other. (You cannot design a highly-advanced 3D-Grafik, if you haven't at least spend SOME money and time on the development of lesser technologies for example).

-When and what you research is all up to you. Just keep in mind, that employees, who are in the process of developing some new technology might be mssing in  the development of your upcoming game. Or you maybe hire some employees just for developing new stuff? It is up to you.

- In reviews of your released games, it will be taken into account, if your used technologies are up-to-date or completely outdatet, as well as if the chosen elements fit your chosen genre. A jump'n run game, which can only be played with a pistol-controller will most defenitly not get the best reviews.

I hope you enjoyed the little insights in this weeks devblog. Next week i will keep you up to date how the development of these system worked and if there where any changes, as well as a new insight in the upcoming weeks workload.

Feel free to share your thoughts, ideas and impressions below this article. I always look forward to new input and feedback.

notes.title: Pre-Alpha 0.12.1 Change-Log
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41321079/ab46a5e0a794e6edd9d8b4086e0229c8a954d47f.png[/img]

[b]Welcome to the first change-log of the internal testing version of Software Company[/b]

It's been a good week since i launched the Steamshop-page  of Software Company. Since then changes on the internal testing version certainly picked up the pace. Here are a few thinsg worth mentioning for now:

[b]New features:[/b]
[list]
[*] - Savesystem is live: In a game where you can spend hours on hours in, you sure need a save system. Good news: It's here!
[*] - Themes: Software Company now provides players with over 130 Themes to give their games a unique touch. Themes further play a role now in the review-score, audience appeal and sales of your games.
[*] - Hintsystem: In Software Company there are quite a few settings, sliders and options to customize your game before starting development. Some settings are more optimal then others, depending on the games genres, themes and developmentfocus. Sometimes it is hard to keep everything in mind, that has to be concidered in your attempt to create the perfect videogame. Good news: Software Company now helps you to remember good combinations, once you discovered them and helps you remeber those good combinations /slider values.
[/list]

[b]Changes:[/b]
[list]
[*] Gamescore calculation: It was far too easy to get a game with a 10/10 rating, when the correct themes where chosen. It is now more balanced.
[*] UI-Refreshment: The overall look and feel of the UI got a bit more slim and cleaned up.
[*] Game-sale calculation: The curve of game-sales was a bit too steep and is far smoother now. Games will sell more even over multiple months, instead of selling almost all copies in the first 2-3 months.
[/list]

[b]Bug fixes:[/b]
[list]
[*] Pedestrians spawned with multiple versions of the character model activeated. This should not happen any more. No more 8-legged monster crawling through the city. Yay!
[*] When closing an in-game menu, the background blur would sometimes not disappear. This should now be fixed.
[/list]
